P01.note: Filtering nitrate while mud and oxygen pass unchanged gives kidney; each distractor has its own planted kill (lung by 'held as much oxygen', net by 'just as brown with mud', kitchen by shrimp guts holding plankton not marsh grass).

P02.note: Few kills but trotting and head-lifting even when the pack was thirty miles away gives cowed; corralled is killed by 'scattered bands', ambushed by 'fewer than thirty elk a year'; chased literally fits the trotting but the pack was absent.

P03.note: Every distractor has a planted kill: rattled by 'unhurried on film', redistributed by 'flights over the timbered slopes found them no fuller', rejuvenated by 'the herd grew older'; once those three sentences are read reduced is the leftover.

P04.note: Scouring walls each spring with nothing lost gives lashed; nibbled is killed by every house of 1700 in use with doorways at builders' height, imprisoned by caravans arriving; lifted is struck on surface (sand does not lift a village; nothing in the passage is about raising).

P05.note: The opening sentence (a strip running twelve miles between two forests, voles in both) hands over corridor before any evidence; cage and cemetery are off-frame for a connecting strip, and 'live as long' plus 'rarely caught twice at the same spot' kill cemetery and cafeteria directly.

P06.note: Fenced corners growing algae while the rest stays cropped makes it a feeding site, canteen; clinic is planted via waving (cleaner) shrimp but the fish swim 'past' them; bedroom killed by water emptying at dusk; ballroom has no direct kill.

P07.note: Tidied, tightened and softened are one family (editing toward polish) and each has a planted kill: misspellings kept, a fifth longer, curses kept; spliced is the only additive option, so the option set itself sorts the item once one kill is read.

P08.note: 'Drove every pony on the common back before them into the village yard' alone gives roundup; pageant fails on 'oldest work clothes', pilgrimage on turning at the stone 'without stopping', raid on families leading home their own notched ponies.

P09.note: Listed, receipted seizure for military use is requisitioned; ransacked fails on the crating and signed list, ransomed on the refused buy-back, repatriated (planted by 'carried off from neighboring towns') on the bronzes going to the foundry and canvases to headquarters.

P10.note: Turnstile and tollbooth fail on a surface read: nothing in the passage concerns counting or charging anyone; only seawall is live, killed by swells rolling over the bar and breaking against the piers, leaving wharf for the cargo transfer.

P11.note: 'A fine lace of shallow grooves' that a wire brush would not remove gives etched; dried killed by matching moisture readings, dislodged by sound mortar, fortified by the gale leaving both halves standing.

P12.note: Customs house, flag and duties gives annexed; blockaded fails on freighters coming and going, boycotted on buyers taking more wool, bombarded on unloading 'as before'. The key is also the only option not beginning with b.

P13.note: Deer kept out gives fence; hearth killed by frost blackening trees beside the wall too, firebreak by the 1791 fire burning the eastern rows, dike by the river a mile away; each distractor is negated by one planted sentence and the plain word survives.

P14.note: 'Vellum and ink bought by the cartload... books in its monks' hand' alone gives scriptorium; sanatorium fails on sick monks carried down to town, tavern on one free night by rule, vault on every book going to the church that paid.

P15.note: Sealed deposits returned unbroken for a fee gives repository; pawnshop is the near miss but nothing was lent against the deposits; pharmacy killed by bottles of lamp oil and whiskey, parlor by barring the door at sundown.

P16.note: Stored oil slowly released through bacteria for thirty years fits battery, but cupboard (a store of food drawn on over time where food is scarce) fits nearly as well and nothing kills it; banquet literally fits the scavengers' first months and is killed only by the thirty-year span.

P17.note: Burial under twelve feet of current-dropped sand gives interred; jostled killed by 'whole and in place', mined is off-topic on a surface read; mummified is the real near miss (preserved from worms) and is undercut only by 'timbers soft and black'.

P18.note: A tenth as many plants and soil washed away gives denuded; fertilized killed by 'tests no richer', furrowed by 'leaving no worn paths', groomed by the bare, sparse cover.

P19.note: 'In reverse order: the harbor at the survey's western end stands at the print's eastern end' hands over flipped, and the copper-plate sentence repeats it; enlarged killed by 'the survey's size', gilded by 'bare of ornament', doctored by 'each at its exact distance'.

P20.note: Banded shrubs eaten while ants are on neighbours 'at every hour' gives patrolled; one sentence ('flowered and podded as heavily, their seeds dropping beneath them') kills both pollinated and propagated, and parasitized fails on unbanded shrubs growing taller.

P21.note: Towns in order up the river with day counts and barley per leg gives roadmap; receipt is planted by the rolled seal and the inn find, payroll fails because the barley feeds donkeys not workers; recipe is struck on surface (amounts plus towns, not ingredients).

P22.note: Columns about the army struck out before printing gives muzzled; nationalized killed by papers staying with founding families, impoverished by sales rising, mobilized by editors leaving blanks rather than filling them.

P23.note: Taller unfertilized corn and doubled topsoil nitrogen gives manured; leached is its opposite and killed by the nitrogen sample, mired by corn going in on schedule, mulched by silt 'too thin to hide the old furrows' and weeds coming up thick.

P24.note: Polished floor plus talc-fine silt (rock flour) gives milled; incised literally fits the parallel grooves but the floor is 'broad and even from wall to wall'; mantled killed by bare granite, littered by 'no loose stone larger than a fist'.

P25.note: Structural cracks, a fence and a no-entry sign gives condemned; bulldozed killed by 'still stands', crated by bell and glass in place, commandeered by 'used by no one'.

P26.note: Discards bricked up with no list and never opened gives dump; depository is planted by the cool dry air and single shaft but fails on 'struck from its catalog' and 'no list'; gallery killed by bricking up, hospital by nothing being restored.

P27.note: Three ships torn open on the barely submerged bow gives tripwire; tomb killed by the crew walking ashore, strongbox by the rails hauled up and sold, trellis by plates kept bare and bright.

P28.note: 'The middle mile was a foot above the height at which it was laid' alone gives raised; rippled killed by 'one long swell', ruptured by 'unbroken', rutted by trucks leaving no mark - the key is the plain literal word with every vivid option negated.

P29.note: The earth bank along the highway and north windows now open gives muffler; junction and mixer fail on visits nearly all from the adjacent row-house blocks, magnet on visits under half an hour by locals only.

P30.note: Clusters halving when honeydew dwindled, with slit empty skins beneath, gives devoured; herded killed by aphids staying on whatever shoot, drugged by walking as quickly on crossed leaves, garnered by nothing being collected or moved.

P31.note: Suppressed small pines died and survivors grew faster, gives winnowed; sapped killed by wider rings and few beetle hosts, scorched by green needles, toppled by the dead staying standing.

P32.note: Image-by-image copying reworded under his name gives plagiarized; pirated is the near miss, killed only by 'every line reworded'; panned killed by the papers naming two among the best; popularized has no direct kill but nothing says they spread.

P33.note: The race taking most of the stream and returning it a mile down gives siphoned; stilled literally fits the mile of trickle but the current below the outlet runs as fast as above; walled killed by a weir 'no higher than a boot', soured by trout as many as the next valley.

P34.note: 'The beavers dig mud from the creek's pools and carry it to the banks' alone gives dredged; flooded killed by no dam and unchanged level, deforested by aspens as thick, greened by both valleys turning the same brown.

P35.note: Chapters cut and sentences stopping mid-clause gives mutilated; lightened killed by the comic chapters being the ones removed and every drowning kept, manicured by the abrupt broken sentences, naturalized by names, fjord and money kept.

P36.note: Flat stones 'each leaning on its downstream neighbor' (imbrication) gives stacked; sorted killed by the same size mix at cliffs and sea, stained by the same shade inside, sanded by broken pebbles still fitting edge to edge.

P37.note: 'Every plank and cask wears a coat of oysters and coral several inches thick' alone gives encrusted; entombed killed by lying on a rock ridge with hatches open, dismantled by hull still where it settled, gnawed by oak hard as the day it was cut.

P38.note: Daily rise at dusk and fall by dawn that the mills run on gives timepiece; storeroom killed by the rise being too small to fill ditches, thermometer by the front holding through warm and cold decades, signpost by no road or path crossing.

P39.note: 'Four lay upright on the sand of a shallow bay' alone gives beached; capsized killed by 'upright', becalmed by the gale, blinded by the moonlit night - each a single planted word.

P40.note: Silt settling, reeds on gravel bars and side channels turned to meadow gives clogged; chilled killed by water drawn from beneath the sunlit surface and bass still spawning, churned by the steady flow, bled by the main channel running deeper.

tells: Kill-every-distractor template: in nearly every item each wrong option is negated by one planted 'as X as / still / no / unchanged' clause (explicit_kills 3 on P03, P05, P07-P09, P11-P15, P18-P20, P22-P31, P33-P40), so the key is found by elimination of three planted negations rather than by reading the passage's positive claim.
Figurative-noun template 'X calls/treats the [place] as the [place's] ______' with four metaphor nouns recurs: P01, P05, P06, P10, P13, P14, P15, P16, P21, P26, P27, P29, P38.
Plain/literal word survives when every vivid option is negated: P13 fence, P28 raised, P03 reduced, P25 condemned.

Near-duplicate worlds: P02/P03 (wolves return to a valley elk herd, 1995/1996), P17/P37 (merchant ship with iron bars and wine sunk, 1690/1790, surveyed by divers in 1990), P07/P32/P35 (a text altered and compared line by line).
The positive clue is often a single late concrete sentence that names the action outright (P05, P08, P14, P19, P28, P34, P37, P39).
